headline: pCloud says a cyberattack on pCloud Pass exposed some users' email addresses; it says stored passwords were not compromised.
summary: New incident page. pCloud's statement, posted in reply to customers on Reddit and reported by BleepingComputer (s001, Nov 27) and The Hacker News (s002, Nov 28), both opened and read: an attack on pCloud Pass, promptly contained; a small number of email addresses exposed and login attempts made; stored data encrypted and not compromised; cloud storage not affected; never asks for Master Password or recovery words. Customers reported new-device alerts, some with two-factor authentication on, some who never used Pass; the alert's link went to a pCloud test address. pCloud has not said how the attackers got in, when, whether any login succeeded or whether encrypted vaults were taken. Main answer Confirmed, filed under hack-stated, on the company's statement as reported by two outlets. incident_type breach; size Local. pCloud has published no notice on its own website. Theory sweep: no Hacker News thread on pCloud in the last seven days; Reddit could not be read. Privacy check done: no customer usernames, addresses or IP addresses carried over.
author: Research agent
